author: claude

patch.value: Likely shape: an --entry-from <field> flag accepting close_reason first, since a closed issue already states its resolution there and the pm CLI records it as part of the close transition. Items without the field fall back to title so no existing repo changes behaviour.
A defect-shaped item title renders backwards under a Fixed heading, and there is no second field to draw the entry from

pm-changelog projects the item title directly into the changelog entry. Issue trackers want a defect-shaped title that names what is wrong, and Keep a Changelog wants an entry under Fixed that describes the change. Those two conventions produce opposite sentences from the same string, so a repo must pick one and be wrong in the other place. This surfaced in review twice in one session with contradictory guidance: pm-linear was told to make a title defect-shaped, and pm-changelog was told the resulting entry describes the defect rather than the fix. Both reviews were right about their own surface. The generator has no field other than title to draw from, so neither convention can be satisfied without breaking the other.

The generator can source an entry from a field other than title, with an explicit opt-in flag and a documented fallback to title when the field is absent; the choice is recorded so changelog check and generation agree; a test proves an item with a defect-shaped title and a fix-shaped alternate field renders the alternate under Fixed

value.author: claude
value.text: Worked around in the immediate case by retitling pmc-n07l to a change-shaped sentence, which matches this repo's existing entries. That workaround costs the tracker its defect-shaped title.

value.author: claude
value.text: Both review findings that motivated this are legitimate on their own surface; the conflict is in the generator, not in either reviewer.

value.author: claude
value.text: When two conventions disagree about the same string, the defect is usually the single string, not either convention.

value.text: Baseline reproduced against the built dist package with a real scratch tracker: closing an Issue titled "The comment-sync test is root-sensitive" with close_reason "Make the comment-sync test independent of the root directory" still emits the defect title beneath Fixed. The canonical whole-tracker read delivers close_reason. Design: explicit --entry-from close_reason (default title), whitespace-only/absent resolution falls back to title; share selection across markdown, summary, structured output and check. Check emits advisory diagnostics for visible closed Fixed items with a recognized present-tense defect title and no usable close_reason; recovery uses pm update <id> --close-reason plus --entry-from close_reason for generation/check.
